request.spec:
A rate may carry a to-date as well as a from-date (RATE_SET gains to=<date> at the end when one
was given; a to-date before the from-date is refused). A rate applies through its to-date; a claim
dated after the to-date of the rate that would apply to it, with no later rate in force on the
claim's date, has due n/a, and everything that reads due follows (a total skips it, a statement
binds n/a, the late charge has nothing to add to).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A rate may carry a to-date as well as a from-date (RATE_SET gains to=<date> at the end when one
was given; a to-date before the from-date is refused). A rate applies through its to-date; a claim
dated after the to-date of the rate that would apply to it, with no later rate in force on the
claim's date, has due n/a, and everything that reads due follows (a total skips it, a statement
binds n/a, the late charge has nothing to add to).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Rates can now have an optional to-date, and all 4 acceptance tests pass with `bin/e2e`.

**Rule I used:** a claim gets the rate with the latest from-date on or before the claim's date. If that rate's to-date is before the claim's date, the due is n/a. It does not fall back to an older rate with no end. For example, with 10% from the start and 20% from 03-05 to 03-07, a claim dated 03-08 is n/a, not 10%. The tests expect exactly this. The "rate % today" column uses the same rule with the sheet's today.

**Stored data:** a new migration, `V29__rate_to.sql`, adds an optional `to_date` column to the rate table.

**Server (`rate/` package):**
- The set-rate request and the rate list now carry `to`.
- A to-date that isn't a valid date, or is before the from-date, is refused. Nothing is saved and nothing is written to the audit file.
- `RATE_SET` gets ` to=<date>` at the end of the line only when a to-date was given.
- Setting a rate again with the same from-date replaces its to-date too. If no to-date is given, the old one is cleared.
- `Rates.find` returns no rate when the rate it picks has already ended. Every server figure gets its rate from it: rollups, totals, statements, settling, closing a period and the late charge. So all of them now show n/a or skip the claim.

**Front end:**
- The rate form has a new to-date field (`rate-form-to`), and the rate list has a To column (`rate-to`).
- `rateOn` in `useRates.ts` uses the same rule as the server, so claim dues, totals, the header, the summary and period figures follow it.

One choice the request left open: a to-date is accepted on a rate with no from-date (one that applies from the beginning of time), with no ordering check.
